question:
The standard deviation of Y is double of standard deviation of x. The correlation coefficient between X and Y is 0.5.

The acute angle between lines of regression is
solution:
The correct answer is **arctan** **(3/5) **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The **acute angle** between lines of regression is given by arctan(b), where b is the slope of the regression line. 
 
• The** slope of the regression** line can be calculated using the correlation coefficient (r) and the standard deviations of X and Y.
 
• In this case, the correlation coefficient is 0.5 and the standard deviation of Y is double that of X, so the slope of the regression line can be calculated as b = 2 * r * (SDy/SDx) = 2 * 0.5 * (2/1) = 2.
 
• Hence, the acute angle between lines of regression can be calculated as arctan(b) = arctan(2) = 3/5.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The relationship between X and Y can be visualized by a scatter plot and a regression line.
 
• The **correlation coefficient** represents the strength of the linear relationship between X and Y
 
 
• with a value of +1 indicating a perfect **positive correlation**
 
• a value of -1 indicating a perfect ** **
 
• a value of 0 indicating no correlation.
 
 
 
• The angle between the regression line and the x-axis is called the acute angle, which is an indicator of the slope of the regression line.
 
• In this case, with a correlation coefficient of 0.5, the relationship between X and Y is moderately positive
 
 
• the acute angle can be found using the tan inverse function, with the result being arctan (3/5).
 
 
 
• The fact that the standard deviation of Y is double of the standard deviation of X means that Y values have more spread than X values
 
 
• the slope of the regression line (represented by the acute angle) helps to describe this relationship.
